Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regent is the Regent of West Bangka.
2. Regional Government is the Government of West Bangka Regency.
3. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services for victims of violence, based in a Hospital, managed jointly in the form of medical care (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
4. Community Social Institution is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and/or other community organizations.
5. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including those in the womb.
6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia who can menstruate and become pregnant or has obtained legal status as a woman.
7. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim;
8. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or is likely to result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life;
9. Violence against children is any act that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom.
10. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
11. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial and/or certain purposes.
12. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing livelihood, care or maintenance in a proper manner.
13. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
14. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
15. Protection for women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecution, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women has occurred or is occurring.
16. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
17. Optimal Service is a dynamic effort consisting of various parts that are regularly related, followed by performance offered by one party to another party by providing benefits, in order to achieve the best purpose.
18. Information is a message (speech or expression) or collection of messages consisting of an order sequence of symbols, or meaning that can be interpreted from a message or collection of messages and can be recorded or transmitted.

Article 3

Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to provide protection and services that include aspects of prevention, services and assistance, reunification and empowerment.

REGENT OF WEST BANGKA

REGIONAL REGULATION OF WEST BANGKA REGENCY

NUMBER 13 OF 2013

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION

FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

BY THE GRACE OF GOD ALMIGHTY

THE REGENT OF WEST BANGKA,

Considering : a. that children and women are creatures created by God Almighty who need to be protected from violence for the sake of their dignity as human beings;

b. that based on the consideration as referred to in point a, it is necessary to establish a Regional

Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection

for Women and Children Victims of Violence;

In View of : 1. Article 18 paragraph (6) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia;

2. Law Number 4 of 1979 concerning

Child Welfare (State Gazette of the Republic of

Indonesia of 1979 Number 32, Supplement to the State Gazette

of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3143);

3. Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning

Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All

Forms of Discrimination Against Women (State Gazette of the

Republic of Indonesia of 1984 Number 29, Supplement to the

State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3277);

4. Law Number 5 of 1998 concerning

Ratification of the Convention Against Torture and

Other Cruel, Inhuman or Degrading Treatment or Punishment

(State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1998 Number

164, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia

Number 3783);

5. Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human

Rights (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia

of 1999 Number 165, Supplement to the State Gazette of the

Republic of Indonesia Number 3886);

6. Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2002 Number 109, Supplement to the State Gazette of the

Republic of Indonesia Number 4235);

7. Law Number 20 of 2003 concerning the National Education System (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2003 Number 78, Supplement to the State Gazette of the

Republic of Indonesia Number 4301);

8. Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2004 Number

95, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia

Number 4419);

9. Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2004 Number 125, Supplement to the State Gazette of the

Republic of Indonesia Number 4437) as most recently amended by Law

Number 12 of 2008 (State Gazette of the

Republic of Indonesia of 2008 Number 59, Supplement to the

State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4844);

10. Law Number 13 of 2006 concerning Protection of Witnesses and Victims (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2006 Number 64, Supplement to the

State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4635);

11. Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2007 Number

58, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia

Number 4720);

12. Law Number 36 of 2009 concerning Health (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2009 Number 99, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of

THE REGIONAL HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES OF WEST BANGKA REGENCY and

THE REGENT OF WEST BANGKA

HAS DECIDED :

To Establish : REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF

VIOLENCE.

Article 2

The Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is carried out based on the principles of respect and recognition of equal human rights and dignity, non-discrimination, gender equality and justice as well as protection of the human rights of Women and Children and the best interests of victims.

Article 10

(1) Every victim of violence has the right to receive protection in accordance with applicable provisions.

(2) Protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out for residents of West Bangka Regency whether committed within the territory of West Bangka Regency or outside the territory of West Bangka Regency.

(3) In addition to protection for victims who are residents of West Bangka as referred to in paragraph (2), protection is also provided for non-residents of West Bangka where the incident occurred within the territory of West Bangka Regency.

Article 6

(1) The Regional Government in implementing protection for Victims of Violence may involve community participation.

(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by individuals, groups or social community organizations.

(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) may be carried out in the form of:

a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against Women and Children;
b. submitting reports to the authorities if acts of violence against Women and Children occur; and
c. providing assistance to victims.

Article 13

(1) PPT must report in writing the implementation of protection for Women and Children victims of violence to the Regent.

(2) Reports as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. administration;
b. finance;
c. services; and
d. performance.
(3) Submission of reports as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out at least once every 3 (three) months.

Article 9

(1) Implementation of Protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner within the framework of PPT.

(2) PPT in handling medical, legal, medicolegal, psychological and economic protection, in its implementation may conduct partnerships with Social Community Institutions engaged in the field of protection of Women and Children.

(3) The implementation of protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) must take into account religious norms, customs as well as the rights and obligations of parents/guardians, husbands and/or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.

(4) The mechanism for handling protection as referred to in paragraph (1) is organized according to Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) and further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 11

(1) Forms of protection provided to Victims organized by PPT in the form of protection:

a. medical;
b. legal;
c. medicolegal (Forensic Medicine);
d. psychological; or
e. economic.
(2) The form of medical protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a, is in the form of treatment and recovery from physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.
(3) The form of legal protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b, is in the form of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
(4) The form of medicolegal protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, is in the form of medical services for the purposes of evidence in the field of law.
(5) The form of psychological protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d, is in the form of assistance in order to restore traumatic conditions including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation to victims and provide psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in solving problems.
(6) The form of economic protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1), is in the form of services for skills and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

Article 7

(1) Social community organizations that participate in the implementation of protection for victims as referred to in Article 6 paragraph (2), are given guidance by the Regional Government.

(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be in the form of social guidance, skills guidance and operational technical guidance.

Article 12

(1) Sources of funds for the implementation of victim protection shall be charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget.

(2) In addition to sources of funds as referred to in paragraph (1), funds may come from other legitimate sources.

Article 15

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation. So that everyone may know of it, orders the promulgation of this Regional Regulation by placing it in the Regional Gazette of West Bangka Regency.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regent is the Regent of West Bangka.
2. Regional Government is the Government of West Bangka Regency.
3. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services for victims of violence, based in a Hospital, managed jointly in the form of medical care (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
4. Community Social Institution is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and/or other community organizations.
5. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including those in the womb.
6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia who can menstruate and become pregnant or has obtained legal status as a woman.
7. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim;
8. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or is likely to result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life;
9. Violence against children is any act that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom.
10. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
11. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial and/or certain purposes.
12. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing livelihood, care or maintenance in a proper manner.
13. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
14. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
15. Protection for women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecution, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women has occurred or is occurring.
16. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
17. Optimal Service is a dynamic effort consisting of various parts that are regularly related, followed by performance offered by one party to another party by providing benefits, in order to achieve the best purpose.
18. Information is a message (speech or expression) or collection of messages consisting of an order sequence of symbols, or meaning that can be interpreted from a message or collection of messages and can be recorded or transmitted.

Article 11

(1) Forms of protection provided to Victims organized by PPT in the form of protection:

a. medical;
b. legal;
c. medicolegal (Forensic Medicine);
d. psychological; or
e. economic.
(2) The form of medical protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a, is in the form of treatment and recovery from physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.
(3) The form of legal protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b, is in the form of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
(4) The form of medicolegal protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, is in the form of medical services for the purposes of evidence in the field of law.
(5) The form of psychological protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d, is in the form of assistance in order to restore traumatic conditions including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation to victims and provide psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in solving problems.
(6) The form of economic protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1), is in the form of services for skills and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

Article 3

Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to provide protection and services that include aspects of prevention, services and assistance, reunification and empowerment.

Article 9

(1) Implementation of Protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner within the framework of PPT.

(2) PPT in handling medical, legal, medicolegal, psychological and economic protection, in its implementation may conduct partnerships with Social Community Institutions engaged in the field of protection of Women and Children.

(3) The implementation of protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) must take into account religious norms, customs as well as the rights and obligations of parents/guardians, husbands and/or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.

(4) The mechanism for handling protection as referred to in paragraph (1) is organized according to Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) and further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 2

The Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is carried out based on the principles of respect and recognition of equal human rights and dignity, non-discrimination, gender equality and justice as well as protection of the human rights of Women and Children and the best interests of victims.

Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or is likely to result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life;
9. Violence against children is any act that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom.
10. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
11. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial and/or certain purposes.
12. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing livelihood, care or maintenance in a proper manner.
13. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
14. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
15. Protection for women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecution, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women has occurred or is occurring.
16. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
17. Optimal Service is a dynamic effort consisting of various parts that are regularly related, followed by performance offered by one party to another party by providing benefits, in order to achieve the best purpose.
18. Information is a message (speech or expression) or collection of messages consisting of an order sequence of symbols, or meaning that can be interpreted from a message or collection of messages and can be recorded or transmitted.

Article 2

The Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is carried out based on the principles of respect and recognition of equal human rights and dignity, non-discrimination, gender equality and justice as well as protection of the human rights of Women and Children and the best interests of victims.

Article 3

Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to provide protection and services that include aspects of prevention, services and assistance, reunification and empowerment.

Article 6

(1) The Regional Government in implementing protection for Victims of Violence may involve community participation.

(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by individuals, groups or social community organizations.

(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) may be carried out in the form of:

a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against Women and Children;
b. submitting reports to the authorities if acts of violence against Women and Children occur; and
c. providing assistance to victims.

Article 9

(1) Implementation of Protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner within the framework of PPT.

(2) PPT in handling medical, legal, medicolegal, psychological and economic protection, in its implementation may conduct partnerships with Social Community Institutions engaged in the field of protection of Women and Children.

(3) The implementation of protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) must take into account religious norms, customs as well as the rights and obligations of parents/guardians, husbands and/or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.

(4) The mechanism for handling protection as referred to in paragraph (1) is organized according to Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) and further regulated by Regent Regulation.

RIGHTS OF VICTIMS

Article 10

(1) Every victim of violence has the right to receive protection in accordance with applicable provisions.

(2) Protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out for residents of West Bangka Regency whether committed within the territory of West Bangka Regency or outside the territory of West Bangka Regency.

(3) In addition to protection for victims who are residents of West Bangka as referred to in paragraph (2), protection is also provided for non-residents of West Bangka where the incident occurred within the territory of West Bangka Regency.

Article 7

(1) Social community organizations that participate in the implementation of protection for victims as referred to in Article 6 paragraph (2), are given guidance by the Regional Government.

(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be in the form of social guidance, skills guidance and operational technical guidance.

Article 11

(1) Forms of protection provided to Victims organized by PPT in the form of protection:

a. medical;
b. legal;
c. medicolegal (Forensic Medicine);
d. psychological; or
e. economic.
(2) The form of medical protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a, is in the form of treatment and recovery from physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.
(3) The form of legal protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b, is in the form of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
(4) The form of medicolegal protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, is in the form of medical services for the purposes of evidence in the field of law.
(5) The form of psychological protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d, is in the form of assistance in order to restore traumatic conditions including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation to victims and provide psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in solving problems.
(6) The form of economic protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1), is in the form of services for skills and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

Article 3

Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to provide protection and services that include aspects of prevention, services and assistance, reunification and empowerment.

Article 9

(1) Implementation of Protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner within the framework of PPT.

(2) PPT in handling medical, legal, medicolegal, psychological and economic protection, in its implementation may conduct partnerships with Social Community Institutions engaged in the field of protection of Women and Children.

(3) The implementation of protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) must take into account religious norms, customs as well as the rights and obligations of parents/guardians, husbands and/or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.

(4) The mechanism for handling protection as referred to in paragraph (1) is organized according to Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) and further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 11

(1) Forms of protection provided to Victims organized by PPT in the form of protection:

a. medical;
b. legal;
c. medicolegal (Forensic Medicine);
d. psychological; or
e. economic.
(2) The form of medical protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a, is in the form of treatment and recovery from physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.
(3) The form of legal protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b, is in the form of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
(4) The form of medicolegal protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, is in the form of medical services for the purposes of evidence in the field of law.
(5) The form of psychological protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d, is in the form of assistance in order to restore traumatic conditions including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation to victims and provide psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in solving problems.
(6) The form of economic protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1), is in the form of services for skills and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

CHAPTER VI

INSTITUTIONS IMPLEMENTING PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 6

(1) The Regional Government in implementing protection for Victims of Violence may involve community participation.

(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by individuals, groups or social community organizations.

(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) may be carried out in the form of:

a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against Women and Children;
b. submitting reports to the authorities if acts of violence against Women and Children occur; and
c. providing assistance to victims.

Article 7

(1) Social community organizations that participate in the implementation of protection for victims as referred to in Article 6 paragraph (2), are given guidance by the Regional Government.

(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be in the form of social guidance, skills guidance and operational technical guidance.

Article 2

The Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is carried out based on the principles of respect and recognition of equal human rights and dignity, non-discrimination, gender equality and justice as well as protection of the human rights of Women and Children and the best interests of victims.

THE REGENT OF WEST BANGKA

HAS DECIDED :

To Establish : REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF

VIOLENCE.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regent is the Regent of West Bangka.
2. Regional Government is the Government of West Bangka Regency.
3. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services for victims of violence, based in a Hospital, managed jointly in the form of medical care (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
4. Community Social Institution is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and/or other community organizations.
5. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including those in the womb.
6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia who can menstruate and become pregnant or has obtained legal status as a woman.
7. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim;
8. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or is likely to result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life;
9. Violence against children is any act that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom.
10. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
11. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial and/or certain purposes.
12. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing livelihood, care or maintenance in a proper manner.
13. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
14. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
15. Protection for women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecution, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women has occurred or is occurring.
16. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
17. Optimal Service is a dynamic effort consisting of various parts that are regularly related, followed by performance offered by one party to another party by providing benefits, in order to achieve the best purpose.
18. Information is a message (speech or expression) or collection of messages consisting of an order sequence of symbols, or meaning that can be interpreted from a message or collection of messages and can be recorded or transmitted.

Article 2

The Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is carried out based on the principles of respect and recognition of equal human rights and dignity, non-discrimination, gender equality and justice as well as protection of the human rights of Women and Children and the best interests of victims.

Article 6

(1) The Regional Government in implementing protection for Victims of Violence may involve community participation.

(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by individuals, groups or social community organizations.

(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) may be carried out in the form of:

a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against Women and Children;
b. submitting reports to the authorities if acts of violence against Women and Children occur; and
c. providing assistance to victims.

Article 3

Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to provide protection and services that include aspects of prevention, services and assistance, reunification and empowerment.

Article 13

(1) PPT must report in writing the implementation of protection for Women and Children victims of violence to the Regent.

(2) Reports as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. administration;
b. finance;
c. services; and
d. performance.
(3) Submission of reports as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out at least once every 3 (three) months.

Article 7

(1) Social community organizations that participate in the implementation of protection for victims as referred to in Article 6 paragraph (2), are given guidance by the Regional Government.

(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be in the form of social guidance, skills guidance and operational technical guidance.

CHAPTER VI

INSTITUTIONS IMPLEMENTING PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS

Article 10

(1) Every victim of violence has the right to receive protection in accordance with applicable provisions.

(2) Protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out for residents of West Bangka Regency whether committed within the territory of West Bangka Regency or outside the territory of West Bangka Regency.

(3) In addition to protection for victims who are residents of West Bangka as referred to in paragraph (2), protection is also provided for non-residents of West Bangka where the incident occurred within the territory of West Bangka Regency.

Article 11

(1) Forms of protection provided to Victims organized by PPT in the form of protection:

a. medical;
b. legal;
c. medicolegal (Forensic Medicine);
d. psychological; or
e. economic.
(2) The form of medical protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a, is in the form of treatment and recovery from physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.
(3) The form of legal protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b, is in the form of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
(4) The form of medicolegal protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, is in the form of medical services for the purposes of evidence in the field of law.
(5) The form of psychological protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d, is in the form of assistance in order to restore traumatic conditions including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation to victims and provide psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in solving problems.
(6) The form of economic protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1), is in the form of services for skills and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

(1) Sources of funds for the implementation of victim protection shall be charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget.

(2) In addition to sources of funds as referred to in paragraph (1), funds may come from other legitimate sources.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regent is the Regent of West Bangka.
2. Regional Government is the Government of West Bangka Regency.
3. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services for victims of violence, based in a Hospital, managed jointly in the form of medical care (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
4. Community Social Institution is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and/or other community organizations.
5. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including those in the womb.
6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia who can menstruate and become pregnant or has obtained legal status as a woman.
7. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim;
8. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or is likely to result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life;
9. Violence against children is any act that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom.
10. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
11. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial and/or certain purposes.
12. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing livelihood, care or maintenance in a proper manner.
13. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
14. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
15. Protection for women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecution, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women has occurred or is occurring.
16. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
17. Optimal Service is a dynamic effort consisting of various parts that are regularly related, followed by performance offered by one party to another party by providing benefits, in order to achieve the best purpose.
18. Information is a message (speech or expression) or collection of messages consisting of an order sequence of symbols, or meaning that can be interpreted from a message or collection of messages and can be recorded or transmitted.

THE REGENT OF WEST BANGKA

HAS DECIDED :

To Establish : REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF

VIOLENCE.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regent is the Regent of West Bangka.
2. Regional Government is the Government of West Bangka Regency.
3. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services for victims of violence, based in a Hospital, managed jointly in the form of medical care (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
4. Community Social Institution is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and/or other community organizations.
5. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including those in the womb.
6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia who can menstruate and become pregnant or has obtained legal status as a woman.
7. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim;
8. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or is likely to result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life;
9. Violence against children is any act that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom.
10. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
11. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial and/or certain purposes.
12. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing livelihood, care or maintenance in a proper manner.
13. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
14. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
15. Protection for women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecution, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women has occurred or is occurring.
16. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
17. Optimal Service is a dynamic effort consisting of various parts that are regularly related, followed by performance offered by one party to another party by providing benefits, in order to achieve the best purpose.
18. Information is a message (speech or expression) or collection of messages consisting of an order sequence of symbols, or meaning that can be interpreted from a message or collection of messages and can be recorded or transmitted.

Article 9

(1) Implementation of Protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner within the framework of PPT.

(2) PPT in handling medical, legal, medicolegal, psychological and economic protection, in its implementation may conduct partnerships with Social Community Institutions engaged in the field of protection of Women and Children.

(3) The implementation of protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) must take into account religious norms, customs as well as the rights and obligations of parents/guardians, husbands and/or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.

(4) The mechanism for handling protection as referred to in paragraph (1) is organized according to Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) and further regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER VII

IMPLEMENTATION AND FORMS OF PROTECTION

Article 10

(1) Every victim of violence has the right to receive protection in accordance with applicable provisions.

(2) Protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out for residents of West Bangka Regency whether committed within the territory of West Bangka Regency or outside the territory of West Bangka Regency.

(3) In addition to protection for victims who are residents of West Bangka as referred to in paragraph (2), protection is also provided for non-residents of West Bangka where the incident occurred within the territory of West Bangka Regency.

CHAPTER II

PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES

Article 7

(1) Social community organizations that participate in the implementation of protection for victims as referred to in Article 6 paragraph (2), are given guidance by the Regional Government.

(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be in the form of social guidance, skills guidance and operational technical guidance.

Article 6

(1) The Regional Government in implementing protection for Victims of Violence may involve community participation.

(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by individuals, groups or social community organizations.

(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) may be carried out in the form of:

a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against Women and Children;
b. submitting reports to the authorities if acts of violence against Women and Children occur; and
c. providing assistance to victims.

CHAPTER IX

REPORTING

Article 2

The Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is carried out based on the principles of respect and recognition of equal human rights and dignity, non-discrimination, gender equality and justice as well as protection of the human rights of Women and Children and the best interests of victims.

Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to provide protection and services that include aspects of prevention, services and assistance, reunification and empowerment.

Article 11

(1) Forms of protection provided to Victims organized by PPT in the form of protection:

a. medical;
b. legal;
c. medicolegal (Forensic Medicine);
d. psychological; or
e. economic.
(2) The form of medical protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a, is in the form of treatment and recovery from physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.
(3) The form of legal protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b, is in the form of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
(4) The form of medicolegal protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, is in the form of medical services for the purposes of evidence in the field of law.
(5) The form of psychological protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d, is in the form of assistance in order to restore traumatic conditions including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation to victims and provide psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in solving problems.
(6) The form of economic protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1), is in the form of services for skills and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

Article 12

(1) Sources of funds for the implementation of victim protection shall be charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget.

(2) In addition to sources of funds as referred to in paragraph (1), funds may come from other legitimate sources.

Article 15

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation. So that everyone may know of it, orders the promulgation of this Regional Regulation by placing it in the Regional Gazette of West Bangka Regency.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regent is the Regent of West Bangka.
2. Regional Government is the Government of West Bangka Regency.
3. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services for victims of violence, based in a Hospital, managed jointly in the form of medical care (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
4. Community Social Institution is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and/or other community organizations.
5. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including those in the womb.
6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia who can menstruate and become pregnant or has obtained legal status as a woman.
7. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim;
8. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or is likely to result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life;
9. Violence against children is any act that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom.
10. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
11. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial and/or certain purposes.
12. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing livelihood, care or maintenance in a proper manner.
13. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
14. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
15. Protection for women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecution, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women has occurred or is occurring.
16. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
17. Optimal Service is a dynamic effort consisting of various parts that are regularly related, followed by performance offered by one party to another party by providing benefits, in order to achieve the best purpose.
18. Information is a message (speech or expression) or collection of messages consisting of an order sequence of symbols, or meaning that can be interpreted from a message or collection of messages and can be recorded or transmitted.

Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to provide protection and services that include aspects of prevention, services and assistance, reunification and empowerment.

Article 2

The Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is carried out based on the principles of respect and recognition of equal human rights and dignity, non-discrimination, gender equality and justice as well as protection of the human rights of Women and Children and the best interests of victims.

Article 9

(1) Implementation of Protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner within the framework of PPT.

Article 11

a. medical;
b. legal;
c. medicolegal (Forensic Medicine);
d. psychological; or
e. economic.

(3) The form of legal protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b, is in the form of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regent is the Regent of West Bangka.
2. Regional Government is the Government of West Bangka Regency.

4. Community Social Institution is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and/or other community organizations.
5. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including those in the womb.
6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia who can menstruate and become pregnant or has obtained legal status as a woman.
7. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim;
8. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or is likely to result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life;
9. Violence against children is any act that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom.
10. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
11. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial and/or certain purposes.
12. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing livelihood, care or maintenance in a proper manner.
13. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
14. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
15. Protection for women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecution, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women has occurred or is occurring.
16. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
17. Optimal Service is a dynamic effort consisting of various parts that are regularly related, followed by performance offered by one party to another party by providing benefits, in order to achieve the best purpose.
18. Information is a message (speech or expression) or collection of messages consisting of an order sequence of symbols, or meaning that can be interpreted from a message or collection of messages and can be recorded or transmitted.

(1) Forms of protection provided to Victims organized by PPT in the form of protection:

(3) The form of legal protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b, is in the form of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
(4) The form of medicolegal protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, is in the form of medical services for the purposes of evidence in the field of law.
(5) The form of psychological protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d, is in the form of assistance in order to restore traumatic conditions including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation to victims and provide psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in solving problems.
(6) The form of economic protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1), is in the form of services for skills and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

Article 7

(1) Social community organizations that participate in the implementation of protection for victims as referred to in Article 6 paragraph (2), are given guidance by the Regional Government.

(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be in the form of social guidance, skills guidance and operational technical guidance.

Article 9

(1) Implementation of Protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner within the framework of PPT.

(2) PPT in handling medical, legal, medicolegal, psychological and economic protection, in its implementation may conduct partnerships with Social Community Institutions engaged in the field of protection of Women and Children.

(3) The implementation of protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) must take into account religious norms, customs as well as the rights and obligations of parents/guardians, husbands and/or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.

(4) The mechanism for handling protection as referred to in paragraph (1) is organized according to Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) and further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 3

Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to provide protection and services that include aspects of prevention, services and assistance, reunification and empowerment.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regent is the Regent of West Bangka.
2. Regional Government is the Government of West Bangka Regency.
3. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services for victims of violence, based in a Hospital, managed jointly in the form of medical care (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
4. Community Social Institution is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and/or other community organizations.
5. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including those in the womb.
6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia who can menstruate and become pregnant or has obtained legal status as a woman.
7. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim;
8. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or is likely to result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life;
9. Violence against children is any act that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom.
10. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
11. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial and/or certain purposes.
12. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing livelihood, care or maintenance in a proper manner.
13. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
14. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
15. Protection for women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecution, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women has occurred or is occurring.
16. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
17. Optimal Service is a dynamic effort consisting of various parts that are regularly related, followed by performance offered by one party to another party by providing benefits, in order to achieve the best purpose.
18. Information is a message (speech or expression) or collection of messages consisting of an order sequence of symbols, or meaning that can be interpreted from a message or collection of messages and can be recorded or transmitted.

Article 6

(1) The Regional Government in implementing protection for Victims of Violence may involve community participation.

(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by individuals, groups or social community organizations.

(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) may be carried out in the form of:

a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against Women and Children;
b. submitting reports to the authorities if acts of violence against Women and Children occur; and
c. providing assistance to victims.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regent is the Regent of West Bangka.
2. Regional Government is the Government of West Bangka Regency.
3. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services for victims of violence, based in a Hospital, managed jointly in the form of medical care (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
4. Community Social Institution is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and/or other community organizations.
5. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including those in the womb.
6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia who can menstruate and become pregnant or has obtained legal status as a woman.
7. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim;
8. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or is likely to result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life;
9. Violence against children is any act that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom.
10. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
11. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial and/or certain purposes.
12. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing livelihood, care or maintenance in a proper manner.
13. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
14. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
15. Protection for women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecution, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women has occurred or is occurring.
16. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
17. Optimal Service is a dynamic effort consisting of various parts that are regularly related, followed by performance offered by one party to another party by providing benefits, in order to achieve the best purpose.
18. Information is a message (speech or expression) or collection of messages consisting of an order sequence of symbols, or meaning that can be interpreted from a message or collection of messages and can be recorded or transmitted.

Article 6

(1) The Regional Government in implementing protection for Victims of Violence may involve community participation.

(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by individuals, groups or social community organizations.

(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) may be carried out in the form of:

a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against Women and Children;
b. submitting reports to the authorities if acts of violence against Women and Children occur; and
c. providing assistance to victims.

Article 3

Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to provide protection and services that include aspects of prevention, services and assistance, reunification and empowerment.

Article 2

The Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is carried out based on the principles of respect and recognition of equal human rights and dignity, non-discrimination, gender equality and justice as well as protection of the human rights of Women and Children and the best interests of victims.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regent is the Regent of West Bangka.
2. Regional Government is the Government of West Bangka Regency.
3. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services for victims of violence, based in a Hospital, managed jointly in the form of medical care (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
4. Community Social Institution is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and/or other community organizations.
5. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including those in the womb.
6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia who can menstruate and become pregnant or has obtained legal status as a woman.
7. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim;
8. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or is likely to result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life;
9. Violence against children is any act that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom.
10. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
11. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial and/or certain purposes.
12. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing livelihood, care or maintenance in a proper manner.
13. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
14. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
15. Protection for women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecution, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women has occurred or is occurring.
16. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
17. Optimal Service is a dynamic effort consisting of various parts that are regularly related, followed by performance offered by one party to another party by providing benefits, in order to achieve the best purpose.
18. Information is a message (speech or expression) or collection of messages consisting of an order sequence of symbols, or meaning that can be interpreted from a message or collection of messages and can be recorded or transmitted.

Article 3

Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to provide protection and services that include aspects of prevention, services and assistance, reunification and empowerment.

Article 13

(1) PPT must report in writing the implementation of protection for Women and Children victims of violence to the Regent.

(2) Reports as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. administration;
b. finance;
c. services; and
d. performance.
(3) Submission of reports as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out at least once every 3 (three) months.

Article 11

(1) Forms of protection provided to Victims organized by PPT in the form of protection:

a. medical;
b. legal;
c. medicolegal (Forensic Medicine);
d. psychological; or
e. economic.
(2) The form of medical protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a, is in the form of treatment and recovery from physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.
(3) The form of legal protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b, is in the form of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
(4) The form of medicolegal protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, is in the form of medical services for the purposes of evidence in the field of law.
(5) The form of psychological protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d, is in the form of assistance in order to restore traumatic conditions including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation to victims and provide psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in solving problems.
(6) The form of economic protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1), is in the form of services for skills and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

Article 10

(1) Every victim of violence has the right to receive protection in accordance with applicable provisions.

(2) Protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out for residents of West Bangka Regency whether committed within the territory of West Bangka Regency or outside the territory of West Bangka Regency.

(3) In addition to protection for victims who are residents of West Bangka as referred to in paragraph (2), protection is also provided for non-residents of West Bangka where the incident occurred within the territory of West Bangka Regency.

Article 7

(1) Social community organizations that participate in the implementation of protection for victims as referred to in Article 6 paragraph (2), are given guidance by the Regional Government.

(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be in the form of social guidance, skills guidance and operational technical guidance.

Article 9

(1) Implementation of Protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner within the framework of PPT.

(2) PPT in handling medical, legal, medicolegal, psychological and economic protection, in its implementation may conduct partnerships with Social Community Institutions engaged in the field of protection of Women and Children.

(3) The implementation of protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) must take into account religious norms, customs as well as the rights and obligations of parents/guardians, husbands and/or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.

(4) The mechanism for handling protection as referred to in paragraph (1) is organized according to Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) and further regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER IV

CHAPTER VI

INSTITUTIONS IMPLEMENTING PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS

Article 10

(1) Every victim of violence has the right to receive protection in accordance with applicable provisions.

(2) Protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out for residents of West Bangka Regency whether committed within the territory of West Bangka Regency or outside the territory of West Bangka Regency.

(3) In addition to protection for victims who are residents of West Bangka as referred to in paragraph (2), protection is also provided for non-residents of West Bangka where the incident occurred within the territory of West Bangka Regency.

CHAPTER X

Article 11

(1) Forms of protection provided to Victims organized by PPT in the form of protection:

a. medical;
b. legal;
c. medicolegal (Forensic Medicine);
d. psychological; or
e. economic.
(2) The form of medical protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a, is in the form of treatment and recovery from physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.
(3) The form of legal protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b, is in the form of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
(4) The form of medicolegal protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, is in the form of medical services for the purposes of evidence in the field of law.
(5) The form of psychological protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d, is in the form of assistance in order to restore traumatic conditions including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation to victims and provide psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in solving problems.
(6) The form of economic protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1), is in the form of services for skills and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

The Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is carried out based on the principles of respect and recognition of equal human rights and dignity, non-discrimination, gender equality and justice as well as protection of the human rights of Women and Children and the best interests of victims.

CHAPTER II

PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regent is the Regent of West Bangka.
2. Regional Government is the Government of West Bangka Regency.
3. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services for victims of violence, based in a Hospital, managed jointly in the form of medical care (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
4. Community Social Institution is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and/or other community organizations.
5. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including those in the womb.
6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia who can menstruate and become pregnant or has obtained legal status as a woman.
7. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim;
8. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or is likely to result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life;
9. Violence against children is any act that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom.
10. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
11. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial and/or certain purposes.
12. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing livelihood, care or maintenance in a proper manner.
13. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
14. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
15. Protection for women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecution, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women has occurred or is occurring.
16. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
17. Optimal Service is a dynamic effort consisting of various parts that are regularly related, followed by performance offered by one party to another party by providing benefits, in order to achieve the best purpose.
18. Information is a message (speech or expression) or collection of messages consisting of an order sequence of symbols, or meaning that can be interpreted from a message or collection of messages and can be recorded or transmitted.
